newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates ease on foreign funds inflow.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates ease on foreign funds inflow.

text.p: Interbank rates eased across a wide front in Kuala Lumpur due to inflow of overseas funds on the back of a strengthening ringgit, dealers said on Tuesday.
They said one-week interbank rate eased to 6.90/7.00 percent against 7.20/25 at close on Monday, while one-month was down to 7.20/25 percent against 7.33/35.
Two-week money was at 7.00/10 percent against 7.25/30, three-week at 7.10/20 against 7.30/35, three-month at 7.25/30 against 7.35/38 and six-month unchanged at 7.35/40.
"Swaps are cheaper this morning, which indicates that foreign funds are coming in. That is pressuring rates downward,' said the head of money dealing at a Malaysian bank.
The ringgit has gained sharply since Monday against the U.S. dollar. It has risen to a four-month high of 2.4940/50 a dollar overnight against 2.5218 at close on Friday.
With the ringgit's sharp gains, more funds are expected to come in over the next few days.
Dealers said higher interest rates in Malaysia, a sharply improved trade balance figure and movement from Singapore dollar to ringgit was helping the Malaysian unit.
The three-month benchmark rate in Malaysia was around four percentage points higher than in Singapore.
"I don't think Bank Negara will be very happy with the fund inflow. It is all hot money which could destabilise the local monetary policy," a dealer with another Malaysian bank said.
Bank Negara has been wary of large fund flows into the economy after it lost several billion dollars in 1993/94 due in stemming hot money flows.
Bank Negara then had to impose capital controls like negative interest rates on foreign deposits.
Dealers said demand for the 10-year government bond continued on Tuesday with prices rising to a high of 100.80 ringgit before settling at 100.75/77 against 100.50/53 previously.
The demand for the bond was both speculative and for meeting reserve requirements. The rise in the price was due to the lack of many sellers in the market.
